newsitem.title: USA: Offshore drilling firms Falcon, Reading & Bates to merge.
newsitem.headline: Offshore drilling firms Falcon, Reading & Bates to merge.

text.p: Falcon Drilling Co. and Reading & Bates Corp. are merging in a deal that will form the world's largest offshore drilling fleet just as oil exploration is increasing in the Gulf of Mexico.

The combined company, to be renamed R&B Falcon Corp., will operate in the Gulf's booming coastal and deepwater oil and gas production zones, with 14 vessels capable of drilling in greater than 3,000 feet of water and 25 jack-up rigs for shallow waters.
Shares of the two Houston-based companies rose Friday after they announced their deal late Thursday night.
Reading & Bates shares gained $2.81 to $33.125 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange, after moving up 10 percent Thursday. Falcon edged up 12.5 cents to $58, also on the NYSE.
Falcon nearly doubled its revenues in the first quarter of this year compared with last year and is converting three salvage ships into drillships to expand its deepwater operations.

Reading & Bates has been positioning for the surge in deepwater Gulf of Mexico drilling, contracting with partner Conoco in June for construction of a second drillship capable of operating in waters up to 10,000 feet deep.

"This combination represents a very significant consolidation opportunity in the fast growing, highest margin segment of the drilling industry -- deepwater," Falcon Chairman Steven Webster said in a statement.
Shareholders will receive one share of R&B Falcon common stock for each share of Falcon common stock, and 0.59 share in the new company for each share of Reading & Bates stock.
Reading & Bates Chairman Paul Loyd will assume that role with the new company. Webster, who is also Falcon's chief executive, will become R&B Falcon's president and CEO.
The deal, which must be approved by shareholders of both companies, is slated to close in the fourth quarter, and the new company's board will include five directors from each company.
Stocks in offshore drilling companies have rallied this year on stepped-up exploration spending in the Gulf of Mexico that is fuelling forecasts of rising rates for offshore equipment.
